stemMd: In Study 1 the students used the same sterilised potting mix, the same growth chamber at $22^{\circ}\text{C}$, the same 16-hour light period and the same number of seeds in every tray. Which of the following best explains why the study was designed this way?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It allowed the mean root length of the seedlings in each tray to be measured to the nearest millimetre on day 10.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It ensured that Variety R and Variety S would reach their highest germination at the same soil water content.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It fixed every condition except water content and variety, so germination differences could be traced to those two.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It guaranteed that every tray, whatever its soil water content, would reach a germination percentage of at least 50%.

explanationMd:
Study 1 deliberately changes two things: the **soil water content** (10%, 20%, 30%, 40%) and the **seed variety** (R or S). Everything else — the potting mix, the temperature, the light period, the seed count, the growth chamber — is held fixed.

That is the logic of a controlled experiment. If the trays had also differed in temperature or in light, a difference in germination could have been caused by temperature or light instead, and the results would not tell you anything about water content. Holding the other conditions constant is what licenses the conclusion that the changes in germination come from the two variables the students chose to vary.

You can check a claim like this by asking what would break if the control were removed. Suppose the 40% trays had also sat under a brighter lamp: their germination figures would then be unusable, because two explanations would fit them equally well. That is exactly the ambiguity the fixed conditions are there to prevent.

distractorRationale.d: Confuses a control with a guaranteed outcome. Standardising conditions does not force any particular germination percentage, and Table 1 shows several groups well below 50% at more than one water content — Variety R reached only 18% at 10% water and Variety S only 40% at 40% water.
distractorRationale.a: Confuses controlled conditions with measurement precision. How finely root length can be read on day 10 depends on the ruler and the technique used, not on whether every tray shared the same soil and light.
distractorRationale.b: States an outcome the data contradict and that no control could produce. Variety R and Variety S peaked at different water contents — R at 30% and S at 20% — and a well-designed study does not force two varieties to behave alike; it makes an honest comparison possible.

accessibilityText: The question asks why Study 1 used identical potting mix, a single growth chamber at 22 degrees Celsius, a 16-hour light period and 50 seeds in every tray, while varying only soil water content and seed variety. The choices, in order, offer more precise measurement of root length on day 10, forcing both varieties to peak at the same soil water content, fixing every other condition so that germination differences can be traced to water content and variety, and a guaranteed germination of at least 50 percent in every tray.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Holding mix, temperature, light and seed count constant leaves only water content and variety varying, so germination differences can be attributed to them. Controls do not determine measurement precision of root length, cannot ensure both varieties peak at the same water content (they did not: S at 20%, R at 30%), and cannot guarantee at least 50% germination (several groups fell below it). [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-cue-batch1-run1) reached the same answer: Holding the mix, temperature, light and seed count constant leaves water content and variety as the only things that vary between trays, so differences in germination can be attributed to those two. Controlling these conditions does nothing to measurement precision. The same optimum for both varieties and a 50% floor are both false in the data: R peaks at 30% and S at 20%, and R reaches only 18% at 10% water.]

review.notes: Author solved the item and attempted to defend each distractor before keying it. Only the choice naming the isolation of the two independent variables describes what standardised conditions accomplish; the others confuse controls with a guaranteed result, with measurement precision, or with forcing the varieties to agree.
